s1.syndrome_frame: Acute collapse with recurrent ventricular arrhythmias
key_facts: Patient is a woman in her 50s
Collapsed at home
Received chest compressions from her husband
Recovered consciousness at home
Vital signs were normal on admission
Physical examination was unremarkable
ECG showed sinus rhythm with normal QRS and QT intervals
ECG showed repetitive monomorphic premature ventricular complexes
Short-coupling interval of 240 milliseconds
Normal serum electrolyte levels
Normal cardiac function and structure on transthoracic echocardiography
No evidence of obstructive coronary artery disease on emergency coronary angiography
Variant of unknown significance in the coding gene of cardiac ryanodine receptor (RyR2)

differentials: Ventricular tachycardia due to coronary artery spasm
per_call: Ventricular tachycardia due to coronary artery spasm

raw.rationale: The patient's ECG showed repetitive monomorphic premature ventricular complexes with a short-coupling interval, which is characteristic of catecholaminergic polymorphic ventricular tachycardia (CPVT). Additionally, the patient's episodes of polymorphic ventricular tachycardia and ventricular fibrillation are also consistent with CPVT.

rejected.label: Ryanodine receptor 2-related arrhythmia
rejected.why: Although the patient has a variant of unknown significance in the RyR2 gene, the clinical presentation and ECG findings are more consistent with CPVT.

rejected.label: Brugada syndrome
rejected.why: The patient's ECG does not show the characteristic ST-segment elevation in leads V1-V3, which is a hallmark of Brugada syndrome.

rejected.label: Arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy
rejected.why: The patient's transthoracic echocardiography showed normal cardiac function and structure, which is not consistent with arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy.

rejected.label: Familial polymorphic ventricular tachycardia
rejected.why: While the patient has a family history is not mentioned, the clinical presentation and ECG findings are more consistent with CPVT.
